title: Alternative Comparison Record
body:
Overview

This record documents Alternative Comparison Record within the Mission Risk and Decision Support Database. Compares alternatives, assumptions, consequences and mitigations. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record lays alternatives side by side under the same criteria, with weights stated openly, and scores each one so the comparison can be re-checked. Assumptions are listed separately from facts, consequences are described before a choice is recommended, and every recommendation carries its mitigations.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: option 1 effectiveness 7 cost 6 risk handling 8 weighted score 6.9. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

A decision maker uses these records to see why one option was recommended, what would change the answer, and what residual risk remains after mitigation. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Alternative Comparison Record: score alternatives on stated criteria with open weights.
alternatives = [('option 1', 7, 6, 8), ('option 2', 8, 6, 6), ('option 3', 6, 8, 7)]
weights = (0.4, 0.35, 0.25)
for name, effectiveness, cost_score, risk_score in alternatives:
    total = round(weights[0] * effectiveness + weights[1] * cost_score + weights[2] * risk_score, 2)
    print(name, "effectiveness", effectiveness, "cost", cost_score, "risk handling", risk_score, "weighted score", total)
best = max(alternatives, key=lambda a: weights[0] * a[1] + weights[1] * a[2] + weights[2] * a[3])
print("recommended on stated weights:", best[0])
print("assumption note: weights are stated openly so the ranking can be re-checked")
demo_output:
option 1 effectiveness 7 cost 6 risk handling 8 weighted score 6.9
option 2 effectiveness 8 cost 6 risk handling 6 weighted score 6.8
option 3 effectiveness 6 cost 8 risk handling 7 weighted score 6.95
recommended on stated weights: option 3
assumption note: weights are stated openly so the ranking can be re-checked

Overview

This record documents Residual Risk Record within the Mission Risk and Decision Support Database. Compares alternatives, assumptions, consequences and mitigations. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record lays alternatives side by side under the same criteria, with weights stated openly, and scores each one so the comparison can be re-checked. Assumptions are listed separately from facts, consequences are described before a choice is recommended, and every recommendation carries its mitigations.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: option 1 effectiveness 7 cost 6 risk handling 8 weighted score 6.9. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

A decision maker uses these records to see why one option was recommended, what would change the answer, and what residual risk remains after mitigation. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked compounded. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: buildable-now. Implementation status: buildable-now. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Residual Risk Record: score alternatives on stated criteria with open weights.
alternatives = [('option 1', 7, 6, 8), ('option 2', 8, 6, 6), ('option 3', 6, 8, 8)]
weights = (0.4, 0.35, 0.25)
for name, effectiveness, cost_score, risk_score in alternatives:
    total = round(weights[0] * effectiveness + weights[1] * cost_score + weights[2] * risk_score, 2)
    print(name, "effectiveness", effectiveness, "cost", cost_score, "risk handling", risk_score, "weighted score", total)
best = max(alternatives, key=lambda a: weights[0] * a[1] + weights[1] * a[2] + weights[2] * a[3])
print("recommended on stated weights:", best[0])
print("assumption note: weights are stated openly so the ranking can be re-checked")
demo_output:
option 1 effectiveness 7 cost 6 risk handling 8 weighted score 6.9
option 2 effectiveness 8 cost 6 risk handling 6 weighted score 6.8
option 3 effectiveness 6 cost 8 risk handling 8 weighted score 7.2
recommended on stated weights: option 3
assumption note: weights are stated openly so the ranking can be re-checked
